definition: Holding an exaggerated, clearly-posed follow-through at the end of a fast action specifically so the viewer can visually register and mentally reconstruct an action that happened too quickly to actually see as it occurred.
purpose: Give the player a chance to retroactively understand a fast action's shape and power, when the action itself was too fast to track in the moment.
visible_effect: A distinct, held, exaggerated ending pose immediately after a fast action, clearly showing the shape, direction, and magnitude of what just happened, even though the action's own motion was too brief to see clearly.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Lets the player's eye catch up after the fact — the brain backfills an understanding of the action from the held follow-through pose rather than from the (unseen) action itself, so the action still reads as clear and satisfying despite being too fast to watch happen.
physical_interpretation: The pose itself is a real physical consequence of the action's momentum (the same inertia the base `follow_through_overlap` principle already describes) — what is new here is treating the HOLD DURATION on that pose as a deliberate readability tool, not just an honest physical consequence.
use_cases: an action fast enough that the player cannot see the motion itself happen frame to frame
any high-speed attack or ability whose shape or power still needs to register even though its motion does not
a player-facing action where responsiveness rules out a long anticipation, so legibility has to be recovered on the back end instead
non_use_cases: an action already slow enough to read as it happens, where an exaggerated hold would just look like an unnecessary pause
a rapid combo or chain of actions where holding each follow-through would break the flow between them
interactions: Follow-through/overlap — this is a deliberate READABILITY use of the same pose the existing card already treats as a weight/inertia signal; the same pose can be doing both jobs at once

Recovery-weight substitution / startup frame budget — a sibling case of the same family: when anticipation is too short to sell power or clarity, both the recovery window (video 3) and now the follow-through pose itself (this entry) can be asked to do that job instead
Arc trail VFX / motion smear readability — sibling readability techniques for a fast action, but those work DURING the fast motion; this one works AFTER it

style_variations.game_combat: the primary context this applies to, especially for the fastest, least-anticipated moves in a kit

cadence_representation: Not represented as a deliberate readability dial, though ordinarily authorable: holding a pose is simply a duration choice on existing keys, ordinary Cadence territory — what is missing is treating "hold duration on a follow-through pose" as a legibility lever the way `anticipation_depth` is a dial for the wind-up side.
control_surface: Ordinary key/timing placement on the follow-through phase; no dedicated vocabulary dimension names this as a legibility control.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Partially measurable: `ai/cal.js PHASE_NAMES`/`ai/plan.js segmentPhases` can locate a follow-through phase and its duration from existing key/marker evidence, the same way it already locates anticipation; nothing currently checks that duration against the preceding action's own speed to judge whether a "backfill" hold is long enough to do its job.
generation_or_modification_methods: None dedicated; a caller would lengthen the hold on existing follow-through keys directly.
failure_modes: a follow-through pose held too briefly to actually register, wasting the technique
holding it so long it reads as a new, separate pause rather than the natural conclusion of the preceding action
applying this to an action that was already readable, adding an unneeded delay
roblox_considerations: None specific — a pure keyframe-timing technique independent of the target engine.
examples: a strong, exaggerated follow-through pose named directly as the way a player "visually registers and mentally backfills" an action that happened too fast to see (video 7 @ 14:01–14:17)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/rYtrV1lChsA @ 13:59–14:17 — Dan states the technique and its purpose directly, over fighting-game footage (Granblue Fantasy Versus) rather than one single named freeze-frame example; experimental until validated
